description: HelixMain MCP tools — the full server surface, 14 tools in TWO groups that are NOT the same card world. API tools (7) are thin clients of the platform API at http://127.0.0.1:3101 carrying a company key; foundry tools (dna.*, 7) run locally on the dna-foundry tree with NO tenant key and are a filesystem trust level, not an API-key one. Names + schemas here mirror dna-foundry/mcp/helix-mcp.js exactly; the dna.* implementations are handlers.py.

tools.name: voice_call
tools.description: Run one turn of a company's card-grounded voice agent: send what the caller said, get the agent's reply. The agent is compiled from the company's DNA card (identity, voice, policies) — it answers only from that card. This is the same turn the AI front desk runs; it does not place a PSTN call.

cardId.description: Card id, if it differs from companyId

tools.name: content_generate
tools.description: Generate a marketing campaign for a company, grounded in its card. Supply either a ready `prd`, or a `goal` plus non-empty `channels[]` (the tool builds the PRD first). Returns the generated per-channel assets. This costs credits (PRD + asset generation).

cardId.description: Card id, if it differs from companyId

goal.description: Campaign goal, e.g. 'fill weekday lunch slots'

prd.description: A ready PRD — skips PRD generation when supplied

tools.name: leads_discover
tools.description: Hunt leads for a company. With lat/lng, uses the OSM/Overpass path (real nearby businesses); with text filters (industry/location/keywords), uses the Apollo path. Returns the discovered leads. Costs credits per hunt.

cardId.description: Card id, if it differs from companyId

size.description: Company size band, if the backend supports it

lat.description: Latitude — switches to the OSM path

lng.description: Longitude — switches to the OSM path

tools.name: site_publish
tools.description: Publish the company's landing page to the public site and return its real URL (https://helixmain.duckdns.org/b/{companyId}/). The page is built deterministically from the card — the card stays the source of truth — and deployed to the web root. Credits are charged only after a successful publish, so a failed build costs nothing.

companyId.description: Company slug whose card drives the site

tools.name: billing_status
tools.description: A company's billing surface. `action=status` (default) is READ-ONLY: credit balance + tier, latest plan, usage history — it spends no credits. `action=config` lists tier/pack prices. `action=checkout` CREATES a real Stripe Checkout session for a `priceId` and returns the API's checkoutUrl verbatim (the one write here); `action=portal` opens the customer portal. No action can mint credits — credits are added ONLY by Stripe's webhook after a real payment, so the API's top-up route is deliberately not exposed.

priceId.description: Stripe price id — required for action=checkout (see action=config)

from.description: Optional ISO date — usage history lower bound

to.description: Optional ISO date — usage history upper bound

tools.name: analytics_query
tools.description: Read a company's analytics for a period. READ-ONLY — spends no credits. With `enriched`, adds campaign/lead roll-ups; note the API computes the enriched lead totals system-wide (all companies), so treat those two numbers as platform totals, not this company's.

tools.name: crm_manage
tools.description: Work a company's CRM. Reads (list/summary/by_stage) and `proposals` are free. `create`/`update` do NOT write — they RECORD a pending proposal (202) and change nothing; `confirm`/`deny` APPLY or discard a proposal and require the owner credential. This is propose → confirm, the same two-step as card edits: an agent drafts, an owner applies. (The CRM store is in-memory, so a proposal can outlive the contact it targets — confirming a vanished contact is an honest 404.)

cardId.description: Card to validate a stage move — for action=update

summary.description: Human summary recorded on the proposal

tools.description: Run the extractor swarm against a business URL (or file:// fixture) and emit a validated, versioned DNA card.

url.description: Business website URL, or file:// path for fixtures

tools.name: dna_extract

tools.description: Fetch a DNA card by id.
tools.name: dna_get

tools.description: Deterministically compile a DNA card into system prompt, policy seed, tool allowlist, and RAG manifest.
tools.name: dna_compile

tools.description: Field-level diff between two card versions.
tools.name: dna_diff
dna_propose_change
tools.description: Propose a governed mutation to a DNA card (field, old, new, evidence, confidence). Low-risk factual updates auto-apply and mint a new version with hash chain + changelog + receipt; identity/voice/policy/competitor changes (and stale proposals) go to awaiting_approval.

evidence.description: Source for the change, e.g. google_listing

tools.name: dna_decide_proposal
tools.description: Approve or deny a pending proposal (dna_propose_change with gate awaiting_approval/conflict). Approval mints the new card version.

tools.name: dna_sense
tools.description: Tiered, cost-efficient re-crawl: Tier-0 change detection (conditional HTTP / sitemap / SHA-256, ~$0.0001), Tier-1 heuristic triage, Tier-2 targeted extraction emitting dna_propose_change proposals, Tier-3 full re-extract on redesign. Adaptive per-site cadence from the volatility sidecar.

tools.name: directory_search
tools.description: Search every business card in the directory (READ-ONLY). Returns matching businesses with the public page a visitor should be sent to. Use this for 'find me a barbershop near me' style discovery. This tool cannot write anything.

query.description: Free text: a trade, a place, or an offering. Empty lists all.
